focus_band: P1 Performance & efficiency (rotated deep dive) + churn-driven pass over everything committed since 2026-07-01 (v0.0.11-v0.0.19: rendering parity, glyph/layout caches, scroll culling, Windows experience)

corpus.notes: The 2026-08-02 automated pass (#204-#232) had already deep-mined P1 across app/paint/text/css/layout/net on this exact HEAD (81255fa, v0.0.19), and the 2026-07-18 pass had enriched #21/#26/#38 with the churn from the parity work. This run therefore verified the corpus against the code rather than re-filing: most fresh candidates traced during this sweep turned out to be covered by an existing issue or an existing enrichment comment. Two genuinely uncovered findings were filed. Prior-run filings #68-#71 are all closed (fixed on main).

findings.title: v0.0.16 glyph bitmap cache clears wholesale at a fixed 4 MiB cap — over-cap visible working sets (HiDPI scaling, CJK-heavy pages) thrash back to full per-frame re-outlining
Mirror windows cannot scroll at all — MultiSurfaceApp has no scroll entry point, MultiState drops MouseWheel, MirrorShell renders pinned to y=0

duplicates_skipped.covered_by: #22 body + 2026-08-02 enrichment comment (collect_computed-per-frame-ungated), which also covers the poll() layout_dirty over-invalidation

duplicates_skipped.candidate: scroll path: display-list deep clone x2 (scaled(1.0) identity clone), translate_items + content_height full rescans, two per-frame framebuffer allocations

duplicates_skipped.covered_by: #38 (implemented by v0.0.16; reconciled in its 2026-07-18 and 2026-08-02 comments; residuals documented there)

duplicates_skipped.candidate: sibling_ref :has() children level clones every element's tag/id/classes/attrs an extra time per cascade

considered_below_bar: Windowed/interactive path hardcodes BlockLayout::default() while headless render() honors CERB_LAYOUT (strangler-fig A/B is deliberately corpus/headless-driven per plan docs — likely by design)
cookie_rows()/mirc_rows() rebuilt+sorted per frame while their panels are open (small N, panels transient)
UA-ladder per-host memo map grows per visited host (tiny strings; bigger unbounded-map issues already tracked: #221 #182 #205)
Rule/Selector specificity recomputed per match instead of cached at parse time (minor vs matching cost, folds into #21's fix)
no_findings_areas: cerberus-net decompress.rs: gzip/deflate bomb-guarded during inflation, header parsing bounds-checked
cerberus-net http1.rs framing: header CR/LF/NUL injection guards present, 32 MiB read cap, chunked-completeness probe only on timeout path
cerberus-image: header-declared-dimension pre-check before pixel allocation, SVG byte cap (post-#52)
cerberus-js-quickjs: heap/stack/interrupt limits landed (closes the #68 gap), watchdog pattern sound
cerberus-app timings.rs: rows cleared per navigation, no growth
cerberus-shell-winit single-window path: Wait control flow, event-driven redraws only
cerberus-css color.rs and resolve_light_dark/substitute_vars/matching_paren: depth-capped, linear, no new hazards found
storage cookie_views: plain clones, no per-frame crypto
overall_health: Good and actively hardening. The July parity/performance releases (v0.0.14-v0.0.19) fixed several long-standing filed issues (layout cache #22-half, glyph cache #38, quickjs limits #68, consent/psl #70/#71), and the 2026-08-02 review wave left an unusually saturated, well-reconciled P1 backlog (#204-#232). This run's honest yield is therefore small: one cache-policy regression risk that silently undoes the v0.0.16 win on HiDPI/CJK workloads (#234) and one functional gap — mirror windows cannot scroll (#235). The highest-leverage open items for the fixer remain #220 (table-DoS cap bypass), #213 (UI-thread JS budget gaps), #210 (no connection reuse), and the #22-residual JS style-push per frame.
